response.justification: The candidate is a broadly experienced, senior-level engineer with genuine geospatial credentials (GISCollective, Green Map web GIS, FOSS4G talk) and some low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems work at Sociomantic/dunnhumby. However, the core requirement — modern C++ (or Rust) systems development — is essentially unmet: the only C/C++ role was a 6-month stint at National Instruments in 2014–2015, with no evidence of modern C++ or any Rust. The last decade is dominated by TypeScript/Node.js web and product work, and there is no experience with routing tiles, navigation guidance, or map data pipelines. Potentially worth a conversation given the strong systems-adjacent D experience and geospatial passion, but they would be a significant ramp-up risk against candidates with direct C++ pipeline experience.
strengths: Real geospatial/GIS product experience (GISCollective, Green Map, FOSS4G)
Low-latency, high-volume microservices work (async I/O, fibers, caching) at Sociomantic
Strong engineering discipline: TDD, CI/CD, testing tooling, Linux/Docker/K8s
concerns: No modern C++ or Rust experience; last C/C++ role was ~6 months in 2014
No navigation, routing, or map-tiling pipeline background
Recent decade is primarily web/full-stack TypeScript, not systems engineering
